items.prompt:
Two folktales both teach 'be kind to strangers.' They share the same:
A) theme
B) author
C) cover

Two tales both end with a greedy character losing everything. They share a:
A) pattern of events
B) different theme
C) setting only

steps: Same plot pattern. Key is A.

items.prompt:
The 'lesson' of a story is its:
A) theme
B) title
C) length

In many tales, the youngest or smallest hero wins. This is an example of a shared:
A) theme
B) pattern of events
C) author

steps: Repeated plot pattern. Key is B.

items.prompt:
A tale from Japan and a tale from Mexico both teach that hard work pays off. They have the same:
A) theme
B) setting
C) characters

Two poems are both about the ocean. They share the same:
A) topic
B) rhyme exactly
C) length

Story A: a clever rabbit tricks a lion. Story B: a clever fox tricks a bear. These tales share a:
A) trickster pattern (a small, clever character outsmarts a bigger one)
B) totally different theme
C) the same exact characters
items.answer: A) trickster pattern (a small, clever character outsmarts a bigger one)

solution.answer: A) trickster pattern (a small, clever character outsmarts a bigger one)

items.prompt:
Why do folktales from very different cultures often share the SAME themes?
A) They explore common human ideas like kindness, greed, and bravery
B) They were all written by one person
C) They have the same setting
items.answer: A) They explore common human ideas like kindness, greed, and bravery

solution.answer: A) They explore common human ideas like kindness, greed, and bravery
